title: Fayum primates of the Jebel Qatrani Formation
summary: Excavations by the Geological Survey of Egypt and Duke University in the Jebel Qatrani Formation, Fayum, Egypt, recovered many primate fossils, including the anthropoids Aegyptopithecus, Propliopithecus, Parapithecus and Apidium, and Qatrania wingi, then the earliest African anthropoid known. A 2006 reassessment placed the youngest Fayum anthropoids between 30.2 and 29.5 Ma and the propliopithecids from about 31.5 Ma.

uncertainty.note: Range from Seiffert (2006); the same paper says most taxa were formerly thought to be 35.4-33.3 Ma. The id says 30 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present.
